# course


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A goal such as “fine-tune my own diffusion model to make Indian comics”
needs more than one walk. A **course** is all that abhyasa has for one
goal: its sources, its **stages** (one walk each), and your answers to
“what do you know already?”.

The course keeps only what abhyasa cannot get again from other records.
“You are here”, “next and why” and “what stands between you and the
goal” come from the walks, the concepts and the Leela results each time
that you ask. So each fact has one place, and no field gets old.

This module has no web page. The `course` block shows it.

- **The record**: one vault document of kind `course` on the learning
  shelf, as a walk is.
- **Join**: a goal walk makes a course, or joins the course of the same
  goal, as its first stage.
- **Where you start**: a few short questions from the model. Your
  answers set where the course starts and how many stages it has.
- **Stages**: the planner gives the stages. The next stage is built when
  the current one is 60% done, or when you open it.
- **The state**:
  [`course_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#course_state)
  and
  [`next_up`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#next_up),
  with eight ordered rules, each with a one-line reason.

Import the shelf, the learner model, the walk engine, the JSON call of
the model and the guard for text that leaves the Mac.

## The limits

`GROW_AT` is the share of a stage that you finish before abhyasa builds
the next stage. `UNCLEAR` is the time in which two boards or explainers
on one idea make it unclear. A course keeps at most `ASKS_MOST` asks,
the newest.


## A goal walk joins a course

A walk that you plan from a goal (`from_goal` in the walk block) is a
**goal walk**: a walk with a goal, no source document, no parent, and
not for a talk.
[`join_course`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#join_course)
gives it a course: the course of the same goal, else a new one. The walk
is a stage of the course, and the walk knows its course (`course`,
`stage`).

[`chip_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#chip_sources)
makes the source rows from the chips of the walk. A chip that did not
file is `failed`, with the line that the walk kept.

### join_course

``` python
def join_course(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, j
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*The course of goal walk `j` (a walk or its id): its own, else the
course of the same goal, else a new one. The walk becomes a stage. None
for a walk that is not a goal walk.*

A small goal walk, as the Start box makes it: two chips, and the clone
of one failed.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
for n, pre in (('Noise', []), ('Denoise', ['noise']), ('Sample', ['denoise'])): lr.put(n, f'{n} a picture.', 'ml', prereqs=pre)
def goal_walk(lr, jid='gw', goal='Fine-tune diffusion for comics', slugs=('noise', 'denoise', 'sample'), **kw):
    return lr.put_journey(dict(id=jid, title='Diffusion for comics', goal=goal, mode='walk', source=None, started=None, created=1.,
                               steps=[dict(slug=s, status='todo', check=dict(way='words', kind='short', depth=2)) for s in slugs],
                               chips=['folder:/x/course22p2', 'gh:huggingface/diffusers'], chip_counts={'folder:/x/course22p2': 44},
                               notes=['abhyasa could not clone huggingface/diffusers.'], **kw))
gw = goal_walk(lr)
```

The walk joins a new course as stage `s1`. The failed clone is a
`failed` source with its line. A second call gives the same course.

``` python
c = join_course(lr, gw)
test_eq([(s['key'], s['walk'], s['status']) for s in c.stages], [('s1', 'gw', 'ready')])
test_eq([(s['root'], s['status']) for s in c.sources], [('course22p2', 'ready'), ('huggingface/diffusers', 'failed')])
test_eq(c.sources[1]['why'], 'abhyasa could not clone huggingface/diffusers.')
test_eq((lr.journey('gw').course, lr.journey('gw').stage), (c.id, 's1'))
test_eq(join_course(lr, 'gw').id, c.id); test_eq(len(lr.courses()), 1); test_eq(course_of(lr, 'gw').id, c.id)
```

A second goal walk with the same goal (case and spaces do not count)
joins the same course as stage `s2`. A side walk joins nothing.

``` python
goal_walk(lr, 'gw2', goal='fine-tune  Diffusion for comics')
test_eq(join_course(lr, 'gw2').stages[-1]['key'], 's2'); test_eq(len(lr.courses()), 1)
lr.put_journey(dict(id='side', title='S', goal='x', mode='walk', source=None, parent=dict(walk='gw', step=0), steps=[]))
test_is(join_course(lr, 'side'), None)
```

[`ensure_courses`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#ensure_courses)
gives a course to an older goal walk that has none, one time.

``` python
l2 = temp_learning(); l2.put('Noise', 'n', 'ml'); goal_walk(l2, slugs=('noise',))
test_eq(len(ensure_courses(l2)), 1); test_eq(ensure_courses(l2), [])
```

## Where do you start

Before abhyasa plans the stages, it asks what you know already: a few
short questions, such as “Do you know how a neural network learns?”. You
answer each with yes, a little, or no, by a tap or by voice. The model
writes the questions from the goal. An idea that you learned already (a
concept at the learned depth) gets the answer yes from the shelf, and
abhyasa does not ask it.

The prompt goes through the guard of ramabana
([`guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/guide.html#guard)), as
the other calls do, so no secret or personal data leaves the Mac.

### ask_level

``` python
def ask_level(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, cid:str, who:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Write the questions of “where do you start” for course `cid` and keep
them on it. Older answers go.*

A fake model writes three questions. You learned Noise already, so its
question has the answer yes from the shelf.

``` python
from abhyasa.llm import Fake
```

``` python
LEVEL = dict(questions=[dict(q='Do you know how a neural network learns?', idea='How a neural network learns'),
                        dict(q='Do you know what noise is?', idea='Noise'), dict(q='Have you used diffusers?', idea='The diffusers library')])
lr.update('noise', floor=4, seen=1)
ask = Fake({'You find out what one learner knows': LEVEL})
c = ask_level(lr, ask, c.id)
test_eq([(q['key'], q['answer'], q['by']) for q in c.level['qs']], [('q1', None, ''), ('q2', 'yes', 'shelf'), ('q3', None, '')])
test_eq(level_done(c), False)
c = answer_level(lr, c.id, 'q1', 'no, never'); c = answer_level(lr, c.id, 'q3', 'a little')
test_eq((c.level['qs'][0]['answer'], level_done(c)), ('no', True))
test_fail(lambda: answer_level(lr, c.id, 'q1', 'banana'), contains='yes, a little, or no')
```

## Stages

[`plan_stages`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#plan_stages)
asks the planner for the stages of the course. It gives the planner your
answers and the stages that have a walk. The planner marks a stage that
teaches the basics as `foundation`, with `skip_if`: the question that
makes it not needed.

Then the rules decide, not the model:

- A foundation stage whose question you answered **yes** is `skipped`.
  It shows, but it counts nothing.
- A foundation stage whose question you answered **a little** is
  `short`: a refresher of 3 or 4 ideas.
- A foundation stage comes before the stages that have a walk. The other
  new stages come after them.
- A stage that has a walk stays as it is. The stages with no walk are
  planned again each time.

So the answers set where the course starts and how many stages it has.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L222"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### plan_stages

``` python
def plan_stages(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, ask, cid:str, who:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Plan the stages of course `cid` with the planner and your answers. The
stages with a walk stay; the others are planned again.*

A fake planner gives three stages for the diffusion goal. The first
teaches how a neural network learns, and is skipped when you answer yes
to `q1`.

``` python
STAGES = dict(title='Diffusion for comics', makes='a LoRA in your comic style', stages=[
    dict(name='How a neural network learns', makes='a small net that learns', ideas=['Gradient descent', 'Loss'], foundation=True, skip_if='q1'),
    dict(name='Diffusion for comics', makes='x', ideas=[]),   # the stage that has a walk: not again
    dict(name='Your comic data', makes='captions.jsonl', ideas=['Captions', 'Image size'])])
ask = Fake({'You find out what one learner knows': LEVEL, 'You plan a course to one learner': STAGES})
def course_with(answer):
    l = temp_learning(); l.put('Noise', 'n', 'ml'); goal_walk(l, slugs=('noise',))
    c = join_course(l, 'gw'); ask_level(l, ask, c.id)
    for k in ('q1', 'q2', 'q3'): answer_level(l, c.id, k, answer)
    return l, plan_stages(l, ask, c.id)
```

A learner who does **not** know how a neural network learns gets the
foundation stage first, before the goal walk.

``` python
l, c = course_with('no')
test_eq([(s['name'], s['status']) for s in c.stages], [('How a neural network learns', 'planned'), ('Diffusion for comics', 'ready'), ('Your comic data', 'planned')])
test_eq(c.makes, 'a LoRA in your comic style')
```

A learner who knows it skips the foundation stage. A learner who knows
it a little gets a short one.

``` python
l, c = course_with('yes')
test_eq([(s['name'], s['status']) for s in c.stages][0], ('How a neural network learns', 'skipped'))
test_eq(c.stages[0]['why'], 'You know it: How a neural network learns')
test_eq(course_with('some')[1].stages[0]['short'], True)
```

## Build a stage

[`build_stage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#build_stage)
makes the walk of one planned stage. It also makes the walk of a skipped
stage when you ask for it, and the stage stays skipped if this fails.
The planner gets a brief: the goal, the stage, its ideas, and the ideas
of the earlier stages, which it leaves out. A step on a concept of an
earlier stage goes, so a stage never asks an idea again. The walk knows
its course and stage, and it reads the sources of the course.

[`due_stage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#due_stage)
says which stage to build now: the current stage when it has no walk, or
the next stage when the current one is `GROW_AT` (60%) done.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L281"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Make the walk of stage `key` of course `cid`, or give the walk that it

### stage_brief

``` python
def stage_brief(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, c, st
)->str:
```

*The goal for the planner of stage `st` of course `c`.*

A fake planner gives the walk of the data stage. It names Noise again,
which stage 1 has, so that step goes.

``` python
PLAN = dict(title='Data', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Noise', statement='n', why='w'), dict(name='Captions', statement='Words for each picture.', why='w'),
                                               dict(name='Image size', statement='An image is 512 pixels.', why='w')])
ask.rules['You plan a learning path'] = PLAN
l, c = course_with('yes')
data = first(s for s in c.stages if s['name'] == 'Your comic data')
sj = build_stage(l, ask, c.id, data['key'])
test_eq([s['slug'] for s in sj.steps], ['captions', 'image-size'])
test_eq((sj.course, sj.stage, sj.goal, sj.title), (c.id, data['key'], c.goal, 'Your comic data'))
test_eq(first(s for s in l.course(c.id).stages if s['key'] == data['key'])['status'], 'ready')
test_eq(build_stage(l, ask, c.id, data['key']).id, sj.id)   # a second call gives the same walk
test_is('Earlier stages teach these ideas, so leave them out: Noise.' in stage_brief(l, c, data), True)
```

### Your data on a course

[`add_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#add_data)
keeps a folder on the course as your data, with a note. abhyasa does not
file it and does not learn from it: the exercises run on it. The walks
of the stages keep the same list, so the notebook of each step in Leela
gets it. A walk that a stage makes later gets it from
[`build_stage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#build_stage).
[`drop_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#drop_data)
removes one folder from the course and its walks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L316"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### add_data

``` python
def add_data(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, cid:str, path, note:str=''
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Keep the folder `path` with `note` on course `cid` and its walks as
your data. A `ValueError` says in one line why abhyasa cannot.*

A folder added as data is on the course and on its walk. The walk that a
stage makes after that keeps it, and the planner sees it in the data
list, with a listing of the folder. A path that is not a folder is
refused.
[`drop_data`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#drop_data)
removes it from the course and from each walk.

``` python
home, old = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(), os.environ['HOME']
os.environ['HOME'] = str(home)
try:
    (home/'episodes').mkdir(); (home/'episodes'/'episodes.json').write_text('{}')
    l2, c2 = course_with('yes')
    c2 = add_data(l2, c2.id, str(home/'episodes'), 'The episodes that my scenarios run on.')
    with ExceptionExpected(ValueError, 'no folder'): add_data(l2, c2.id, '~/nothing')
    j2 = build_stage(l2, ask, c2.id, first(s for s in c2.stages if s['name'] == 'Your comic data')['key'])
finally: os.environ['HOME'] = old
mine = [dict(path='~/episodes', note='The episodes that my scenarios run on.')]
test_eq((c2.data, l2.journey('gw').data, j2.data), (mine, mine, mine))
assert '- EPISODES: The episodes that my scenarios run on. It holds: episodes.json.' in first(p for p, sp in reversed(ask.calls) if 'You plan a learning path' in p + sp)
c2 = drop_data(l2, c2.id, '~/episodes')
test_eq((c2.data, l2.journey('gw').data, l2.journey(j2.id).data), ([], [], []))
```

A skipped stage stays skipped when its build fails. Here the planner
gives only Noise again, so the stage gets no new ideas.

``` python
sl, sc = course_with('yes')
k0 = sc.stages[0]['key']
ask.rules['You plan a learning path'] = dict(title='Nets', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Noise', statement='n', why='w')])
test_fail(lambda: build_stage(sl, ask, sc.id, k0), contains='no new ideas')
test_eq({k: sl.course(sc.id).stages[0][k] for k in ('status', 'why')}, dict(status='skipped', why='You know it: How a neural network learns'))
```

When the build of a skipped stage works, the stage gets its walk and is
ready.

``` python
ask.rules['You plan a learning path'] = dict(title='Nets', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Loss', statement='How wrong the net is.', why='w')])
test_eq((build_stage(sl, ask, sc.id, k0).stage, sl.course(sc.id).stages[0]['status']), (k0, 'ready'))
ask.rules['You plan a learning path'] = PLAN
```

## The state of a course

[`stage_rows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#stage_rows)
gives each stage with its walk, its counts and one state word: `done`,
[`ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/model.html#ready) (it
has a walk, and ideas to learn), `planned`, `building`, `skipped`, or
`known`. A planned stage whose ideas you learned in the meantime is
`known`: the plan changes when what you show in checks changes. The
**current stage** is the first stage that is
[`ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/model.html#ready),
`planned` or `building`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L338"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### due_stage

``` python
def due_stage(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, c, rows:NoneType=None
)->str | None:
```

*The key of the stage to build now: the current stage when it has no
walk, else the next planned stage when the current one is `GROW_AT`
done.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L323"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### stage_rows

``` python
def stage_rows(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, c, by:dict=None
)->list:
```

*Each stage of course `c` with `n`, its walk `j`, its
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#walk_state)
`ws`, `done`, `total` and `state`.*

The data stage has a walk now. Stage 1 is skipped. Stage 2 (the goal
walk) is current and less than 60% done, so
[`due_stage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#due_stage)
names nothing to build.

``` python
rows = stage_rows(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq([(r.n, r.state) for r in rows], [(1, 'skipped'), (2, 'ready'), (3, 'ready')])
test_eq(due_stage(l, l.course(c.id)), None)
```

In the course of a learner who said no, the foundation stage is current
and has no walk, so it is due at once. A planned stage whose ideas you
learned is `known`.

``` python
l, c = course_with('no')
test_eq(due_stage(l, c), 's2')
for n in ('Gradient descent', 'Loss'): l.put(n, n, 'ml'); l.update(l.concepts().filter(lambda x: x.name == n)[0].slug, floor=4, seen=1)
test_eq(stage_rows(l, c)[0].state, 'known'); test_eq(due_stage(l, c), None)
```

## What to learn next, and why

[`next_up`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#next_up)
gives one thing to do and one reason. The first rule that gives a thing
wins:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>#</th>
<th>rule</th>
<th>reason</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>Leela filed a failed check on an idea of the current stage</td>
<td>“Your notebook did not pass. Look at the error first.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>A review is due for an idea that the current stage needs, and its
recall is under <code>review.fading</code></td>
<td>“Review Softmax first. The next idea needs it, and you start to
forget it.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3</td>
<td>You asked about an idea of the stage two or more times in two days
(boards, explainers), with no right check since</td>
<td>“You asked about alpha bar two times. Check it now.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>The next idea is ready: you know the ideas that it needs</td>
<td>“Next: Add noise at step t. You know the ideas that it needs.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5</td>
<td>The next idea is not ready</td>
<td>“Next: Derivatives first. Add noise at step t needs it.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6</td>
<td>The current stage has no walk, and you are weak on an idea that it
needs</td>
<td>“Practice Guidance. Stage 4 builds on it.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7</td>
<td>The current stage has no walk yet</td>
<td>“Stage 3 is next: Your comic data. It makes captions.jsonl.”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8</td>
<td>All stages are done</td>
<td>“You reached your goal.”</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Rules for all: only one review before a new idea, so the course moves (a
review since the last idea that you finished turns rule 2 off). A demo
or an explainer never counts as learned. When you opened an idea that is
not the first one to learn, it wins once, and the reason says “You
opened this idea last, so you go on from it.”

`go` says where the button goes: `{kind: 'step', walk, step}`,
`{kind: 'review', slug}`, `{kind: 'stage', key}` or `{kind: 'done'}`.
The block makes the link.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L401"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### next_up

``` python
def next_up(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, c, rows:NoneType=None, by:dict=None, now:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The one thing to do next in course `c`: `rule`, `why` (one line),
`slug`, `name`, `stage` and `go`.*

### Each rule, with a small course

`fixture` makes a course with one goal walk of three ideas: Noise, then
Denoise (it needs Noise), then Sample (it needs Denoise). `done(i)`
marks idea `i` done, with its concept at depth 4.

``` python
def fixture():
    l = temp_learning()
    for n, pre in (('Noise', []), ('Denoise', ['noise']), ('Sample', ['denoise'])): l.put(n, f'{n} a picture.', 'ml', prereqs=pre)
    goal_walk(l); c = join_course(l, 'gw')
    return l, c
def done(l, i, at=None):
    slug = l.journey('gw').steps[i]['slug']
    l.walk_step('gw', i, done=dict(outcome='solid', at=at or time.time())); l.update(slug, floor=4, seen=1, last=time.time(), stability=5., due=time.time() + 5 * 86400)
```

**Rule 4.** Two ideas are done, so you are at idea 3, and you know what
it needs.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); done(l, 1)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.slug, nx.go), (4, 'sample', dict(kind='step', walk='gw', step=2)))
test_eq(nx.why, 'Next: Sample. You know the ideas that it needs.')
```

**Rule 4, you chose it.** You opened idea 3 while idea 2 is still to
learn. Your pick wins, with its reason.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); l.update('denoise', floor=3)   # Denoise is ready to build on, but not learned
l.merge_course(c.id, here=dict(walk='gw', step=2, slug='sample', at=time.time()))
test_eq((next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).slug, next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).why), ('sample', 'You opened this idea last, so you go on from it.'))
```

**Rule 5.** Nothing is done, and idea 2 is next when you skip idea 1:
Denoise needs Noise, which you do not know.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); l.walk_step('gw', 0, done=dict(outcome='skipped', at=time.time()))
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.slug, nx.why), (5, 'denoise', 'Next: Noise first. Denoise needs it.'))
```

**Rule 1.** Leela filed a failed check for idea 3. That comes first.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); done(l, 1)
l.record('sample', 'Run the tests', correct=False, kind='code', app='leela', walk='gw', step=2)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.go['step'], nx.why), (1, 2, 'Your notebook did not pass. Look at the error first.'))
```

**Rule 2.** Denoise is done, Sample needs it, and its review is due with
a low recall. After one review, the course moves on.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0, at=time.time() - 20 * 86400); done(l, 1, at=time.time() - 20 * 86400)
l.update('denoise', last=time.time() - 30 * 86400, stability=1., due=time.time() - 86400)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.go, nx.why), (2, dict(kind='review', slug='denoise'), 'Review Denoise first. The next idea needs it, and you start to forget it.'))
l.record('denoise', 'What does denoise do?', correct=True)
test_eq(next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).rule, 4)
```

[`add_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#add_ask)
keeps one ask on the course: a board of the screen guide, an explainer,
a demo or a notebook. It keeps only the words that you said, the idea
and the time, never the page.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L427"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### add_ask

``` python
def add_ask(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, cid:str, where:str, slug:str, kind:str, said:str='', ref:str='', outcome:str='',
    at:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Keep one ask on course `cid`: `where` (walk, session or guide), the
idea `slug`, its `kind`, your words
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#said). At most
`ASKS_MOST`, the newest.*

**Rule 3.** You asked the screen guide about idea 3 two times. A right
check after the last ask clears it.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); done(l, 1)
for _ in range(2): add_ask(l, c.id, 'guide', 'sample', 'board', said='what is sampling?', at=time.time() - 60)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id))
test_eq((nx.rule, nx.why), (3, 'You asked about Sample two times. Check it now.'))
l.record('sample', 'Sample one picture', correct=True)
test_eq(next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).rule, 4)
test_fail(lambda: add_ask(l, c.id, 'guide', 'sample', 'page'), contains='kind of ask')
```

**Rules 6, 7 and 8.** With the goal walk done and a planned stage after
it, the next stage comes, after a weak idea that it needs. With no stage
left, you reached your goal.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); [done(l, i) for i in range(3)]
l.change_course(c.id, lambda c: c.stages.append(dict(key='s2', name='Your comic data', makes='captions.jsonl', ideas=['Sample', 'Captions'], walk=None, status='planned')))
test_eq(next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).why, 'Stage 2 is next: Your comic data. It makes captions.jsonl.')
l.update('sample', misses=2)
nx = next_up(l, l.course(c.id)); test_eq((nx.rule, nx.why), (6, 'Practice Sample. Stage 2 builds on it.'))
l.change_course(c.id, lambda c: c.stages.pop())
test_eq(next_up(l, l.course(c.id)).why, 'You reached your goal.')
```

### What stands between you and the goal

[`blocking`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#blocking)
gives the rows, in this order, each with a line and one action:

- **idea**: the ideas still to learn in the stages that are not
  finished;
- **weak**: an idea that you learned, that is weak now, and that a stage
  still to do needs;
- **notebook**: notebook ideas with no passed check from Leela;
- **setup**: Leela is not running (when the block knows it,
  `leela=False`), or a notebook has no folder for its data;
- **source**: a source that failed or still files, ideas that research
  still looks for, and a stage with no passage for half of its ideas.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L437"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### blocking

``` python
def blocking(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, c, rows:NoneType=None, by:dict=None, leela:bool=None, now:float=None
)->list:
```

*The rows of “what stands between you and the goal”:
`{kind, line, act, go}`, in the order of the kinds.*

A failed clone shows a `source` row. A notebook idea with Leela off
shows a `notebook` row and a `setup` row, and its empty data folder a
second `setup` row.

``` python
l, c = fixture()
l.walk_slug('gw', 'sample', check=dict(way='code', kind='notebook', depth=4), nb=dict(data=[dict(name='comics', what='your comic images', path='')]))
bs = blocking(l, l.course(c.id), leela=False)
test_eq([b.kind for b in bs], ['idea', 'notebook', 'setup', 'setup', 'source', 'source'])
test_eq(bs[0].line, '3 ideas: Noise, Denoise, Sample.')
test_eq([b.line for b in bs[1:5]], ['1 notebook to run in Leela: Sample.', 'Leela is not running. Start Leela to run the notebooks.',
                                    'Set the folder of your comic images.', 'abhyasa could not clone huggingface/diffusers.'])
test_eq(bs[5].line, 'Stage 1: 3 ideas have no source yet.')
```

### [`course_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#course_state)

[`course_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#course_state)
puts it together for the page, with no write: the course, the stages,
the current stage, “you are here”, the counts over all stages (a planned
stage counts by its plan), next and why, the blocking rows, what you
made in Leela, and `finished`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L464"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### course_state

``` python
def course_state(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, cid:str, leela:bool=None, now:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*Where you are in course `cid`, what comes next and why, and what stands
between you and the goal. It writes nothing. None for an unknown
course.*

The state of the fixture after two ideas: you are at idea 3 of 3 in
stage 1, and two of three ideas are done.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0); done(l, 1)
st = course_state(l, c.id)
test_eq((st.here.n, st.here.of, st.here.stage, st.here.name), (3, 3, 1, 'Sample'))
test_eq((st.done, st.total, st.next.rule, st.finished), (2, 3, 4, False))
done(l, 2); test_eq(course_state(l, c.id).finished, True)
test_is(course_state(l, 'none'), None)
```

## Known ideas

An idea that you learned in a session or in another walk counts: it
shows “known (learned elsewhere)”, it asks nothing, and its review comes
when it is due. Here you learn Denoise in a session. The course counts
it, and “you are here” goes past it.

``` python
l, c = fixture(); done(l, 0)
l.update('denoise', floor=4, seen=1)   # a session closed Denoise at depth 4
st = course_state(l, c.id)
test_eq([s.dot for s in st.stages[0].ws.steps], ['done', 'known', 'now'])
test_eq((st.stages[0].ws.steps[1].elsewhere, st.done, st.here.name), (True, 2, 'Sample'))
```

A new goal walk marks an idea that you learned as `known` when it is
made, so it never asks it.

``` python
l = temp_learning(); l.put('Noise', 'n', 'ml'); l.update('noise', floor=4, seen=1)
wj = walk_from_topic(l, Fake({'You plan a learning path': dict(title='T', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Noise', statement='n', why='w', slug='noise'), dict(name='Captions', statement='Captions are words for each picture.', why='w')])}), 'Make comics')
test_eq([s['status'] for s in wj.steps], ['known', 'todo'])
```

## Where you are

[`set_here`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#set_here)
keeps the last idea that you opened in a walk of the course. It writes
only when the idea changed, or after a minute, so a page that loads
again does not write each time.
[`active_course`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/course.html#active_course)
is the course that you used last, for Today.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/course.py#L490"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning

```

*The course that you used last: the newest `here`, else the newest
course.*

### set_here

``` python
def set_here(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, j, i:int, now:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*Keep step `i` of walk `j` as the place where you are in its course.
None when the walk is in no course.*

``` python
l, c = fixture()
test_eq(set_here(l, l.journey('gw'), 1).here['slug'], 'denoise')
v = l.course(c.id).v; set_here(l, l.journey('gw'), 1); test_eq(l.course(c.id).v, v)   # the same idea: no write
test_eq(active_course(l).id, c.id)
```
